questions.question: FIFO stands for?
questions.explanation: Oldest stock ships first, preventing ageing of grease and packaging.

questions.question: Cycle counting means?
questions.explanation: Small portions of stock are counted regularly to keep records accurate.

questions.question: In ABC analysis, 'A' items are?
questions.explanation: A items are few but make up most of the value, so they get the tightest control.

questions.question: Safety stock protects against?
questions.explanation: Buffer stock covers forecast errors and supplier delays to keep service high.

questions.question: Dead stock is stock that?
questions.explanation: Non-moving stock ties up cash and space and may need disposal.

questions.question: EOQ balances ordering cost and?
questions.explanation: Economic Order Quantity minimises total ordering plus carrying cost.

questions.question: Reorder point = lead-time demand + ?
questions.explanation: Reorder when stock falls to expected lead-time usage plus safety stock.

questions.question: In VMI, who manages the stock?
questions.explanation: In Vendor Managed Inventory the supplier monitors and refills the customer's stock.

questions.question: WMS stands for?
questions.explanation: A Warehouse Management System tracks bins, picking, packing and stock in real time.

questions.question: How should bearings be stored?
questions.explanation: Keep bearings in original packs, off the floor, in a dry and clean area.

questions.question: Cross-docking means goods are?
questions.explanation: Incoming goods go straight to outbound trucks with little or no storage time.

questions.question: Fixed bin locations help to?
questions.explanation: Each item has an address so pickers find it quickly and accurately.

questions.question: FEFO ships which stock first?
questions.explanation: First-Expiry-First-Out ships items with shelf-life limits, like greases, first.

questions.question: Stacking cartons too high causes?
questions.explanation: Overstacking crushes lower cartons and can damage bearings or topple stacks.

questions.question: A milk run means one truck?
questions.explanation: A milk run picks up from several nearby suppliers on a fixed route and schedule.

questions.question: Major seaport serving Chennai plants?
questions.explanation: Chennai Port and nearby Kamarajar (Ennore) Port handle most of the region's containers.

questions.question: One TEU equals one?
questions.explanation: One TEU is one twenty-foot container; a 40-ft container is two TEU.

questions.question: An LCL shipment means?
questions.explanation: Less than Container Load cargo shares a container with other shippers.

questions.question: E-way bill is needed for goods above?
questions.explanation: GST rules require an e-way bill for moving goods worth over ₹50,000.

questions.question: VCI paper in bearing packs prevents?
questions.explanation: Volatile Corrosion Inhibitor paper releases vapour that protects steel from rust.

questions.question: Wooden export pallets need which mark?
questions.explanation: ISPM-15 requires heat treatment or fumigation of wood packaging to stop pests.

questions.question: Container kept at port too long incurs?
questions.explanation: Demurrage is charged for containers kept in port beyond the free time.

questions.question: An air waybill is used for?
questions.explanation: The air waybill is the transport contract and receipt for air freight.

questions.question: A bill of lading is issued for?
questions.explanation: A bill of lading is the carrier's receipt and title document for sea cargo.

questions.question: 3PL stands for?
questions.explanation: A 3PL provider handles warehousing or transport for a company.

questions.question: POD in delivery stands for?
questions.explanation: Proof of Delivery is the customer's signed acknowledgement of receipt.

questions.question: Reverse logistics handles what?
questions.explanation: Reverse logistics manages returned, rejected or recyclable goods coming back.

questions.question: HSN heading for ball & roller bearings?
questions.explanation: HSN heading 8482 covers ball and roller bearings for GST and customs.

questions.question: Import customs document in India?
questions.explanation: The Bill of Entry is filed with customs to clear imported goods.

questions.question: Export customs document in India?
questions.explanation: The Shipping Bill is filed with customs for export clearance.

questions.question: Incoterm with the least seller duty?
questions.explanation: Under Ex Works the buyer collects from the seller and bears nearly all cost and risk.

questions.question: Incoterm with the most seller duty?
questions.explanation: Delivered Duty Paid makes the seller pay transport, duties and taxes to destination.

questions.question: Incoterms edition currently in use?
questions.explanation: Incoterms 2020 is in force, with 11 rules including DPU, which replaced DAT.

questions.question: Under FOB, risk passes when goods are?
questions.explanation: Under FOB, risk moves to the buyer once goods are loaded on board the vessel.

questions.question: A licensed customs broker is called?
questions.explanation: Customs House Agents (customs brokers) file documents and clear cargo for traders.

questions.question: S&OP balances demand with?
questions.explanation: Sales & Operations Planning aligns forecasts with capacity, stock and purchasing.

questions.question: Forecast error is often measured by?
questions.explanation: Mean Absolute Percentage Error shows how far forecasts were from actual demand.

questions.question: Lead time is the time from order to?
questions.explanation: Lead time is how long it takes to receive goods after ordering them.

questions.question: Bullwhip effect: demand swings do what?
questions.explanation: Small changes at customers amplify into big swings for suppliers further upstream.

questions.question: Budget vs actual difference is called?
questions.explanation: Variance analysis explains why actual results differ from the budget.

questions.question: India's financial year runs?
questions.explanation: Indian companies follow an April–March financial year.

questions.question: DSI shows the days needed to?
questions.explanation: Days Sales of Inventory shows how long stock sits before being sold.

questions.question: Cash cycle = DSI + DSO − ?
questions.explanation: The cash conversion cycle adds stock and receivable days, minus payable days.

questions.question: Inventory turns = COGS ÷ ?
questions.explanation: Higher turns mean stock moves faster and less cash is tied up.

questions.question: Standard vs actual cost gap is a?
questions.explanation: Cost variances show where material, labour or overhead overshot standard.

questions.question: NSK is listed in Japan, so units follow?
questions.explanation: Japan's J-SOX rules require internal control reporting across a listed group.

questions.question: Segregation of duties prevents what?
questions.explanation: Splitting order, receipt and payment duties stops one person controlling a whole process.

questions.question: Example of a cost centre in a plant?
questions.explanation: Cost centres collect costs of departments like maintenance for control and allocation.

questions.question: Transfer pricing rules apply to deals with?
questions.explanation: Cross-border deals between group companies must be priced at arm's length.

questions.question: Writing off obsolete stock reduces?
questions.explanation: Writing off non-moving stock is an expense that reduces profit for the period.
